# HSkeleton

> Text, rectangle, and circular loading placeholders with reduced-motion support.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This describes repository source for version 0.4.0. Match documentation to your installed source/release.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HSkeleton` from `@hearth-ui/vue`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-skeleton>`.
- Constructor: `HearthSkeletonElement` from `@hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Feedback.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HSkeleton.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- Shapes are text, rectangle, and circle. Text lines are bounded to 1–20. width/height are CSS strings.
- The label creates a loading status. Use label="" for decorative instances when another loading announcement already exists.
- Animation respects prefers-reduced-motion. Replace skeletons with actual content when ready.

## Public API

variant: text | rectangle | circle · lines: number (1–20) · width, height, label: string · animated: boolean

A `?` marks optional source props. Props with defaults may be omitted. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    variant?: "text" | "rectangle" | "circle";
    lines?: number;
    width?: string;
    height?: string;
    label?: string;
    animated?: boolean;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{
    variant: "text",
    lines: 3,
    label: "Loading content",
    animated: true,
  }
```

### Events

None

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose argument arrays in `event.detail`. Listen on the element. Native events such as `click` retain their normal payloads. The elements package provides framework-independent DOM event types.

### Slots

None

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Web components do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, block

Use `hearth-skeleton::part(part-name)` for an exposed part or inherited `--h-*` tokens for shared styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { HSkeleton } from '@hearth-ui/vue';
import '@hearth-ui/vue/styles.css';

</script>

<template>
  <HSkeleton variant="text" :lines="3" label="Loading applications" />
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point. For field submission, use an owning native form; the auth page already contains its own form.

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

This is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Initial array/object properties are assigned before connection to establish reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@hearth-ui/elements';
import '@hearth-ui/elements/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-skeleton');
Object.assign(element, {
  "variant": "text",
  "lines": 3,
  "label": "Loading applications"
});

mount.append(element);
```
